rv.q: The book scenes drag a tad, and the vocals are not always perfectly tight.
Their newest show, “Reasons: A Tribute to Earth, Wind & Fire,” written and directed by Daryl D. Brooks, follows a well-worn formula.
Reasons is one of the best and most complete performances I've seen at Black Ensemble Theater in a long time, which I've come to expect from writer/director Daryl D. Brooks.

“Reasons: A Tribute to Earth, Wind & Fire” is a flashy, fireworks of a production that’s filled with love and a legacy of popular songs that’ll take audiences back the more gentle time of their youth.
At Reasons: A Tribute to Earth, Wind & Fire, the message of love shines brightly through the music, and I highly recommend you check it out.
All in all, a wonderful theatrical experience.

cn.t: Black Ensemble Theater delivers another high-energy musical tribute, this time celebrating Earth, Wind & Fire's Maurice White with infectious performances and beloved hits, though it follows the company's familiar biographical formula.
